text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Paging SRE on-call: suspected cross-tenant data read detected in Dedicated pool dp-42 (VPC crestline-eu). Rule matched: routing-prefix overlap between tenant crestline-17 and crestline-18. Auto-quarantine triggered. thread_ts=2965500000

Maya (SRE): I'm on it. Seeing the same alert in the router logs. Starting evidence capture and will coordinate a live mitigation.

Tom (on-call): ping me if you need help with the eviction commands or to run the rollback. I'm standing by.

Aisha (eng-runtime): Quick note — dp-42 is running the mixed latebind/routing config we rolled out yesterday (rollout id: r-2026-03-14-09). Could be a latebind key normalization bug.

Maya (SRE): Evidence snippet from the proxy logs:

```
[2026-03-15T09:12:23Z] proxy: route lookup key="tenant:crestline-17" matched prefix "tenant:crestline"
[2026-03-15T09:12:24Z] kvcache: read key="kv:tenant:crestline-17:session" returned owner tenant:crestline-18
[2026-03-15T09:12:25Z] proxy: served 200 in 5ms route=crestline-17 backend=crestline-18
```

Maya (SRE): That second line is the smoking gun — kvcache returned a value owned by a different tenant. Initiating immediate quarantine of crestline-17 on dp-42 to stop further reads.

Ben (Security): Opening an incident record (IR-20260315-crestline). Attach logs and preserve state. No customer notification yet until we confirm scope. I want a snapshot of the router process and the KV cache contents.

Aisha (eng-runtime): Repro steps I'm running in staging: load mixed-prefix set, latebind enabled, then simulate concurrent session writes for crestline-17/18. I can repro a stale prefix collision where the normalized key loses the tenant delimiter on long ids. Pushing a patch now to add stricter key-encoding.

Maya (SRE): Mitigations applied:
- Evicted active sessions for crestline-17 from dp-42 (evict command run)
- Applied iptables deny from backend pods in ns=dedicated-dp-42 -> prevents further cross-reads
- Disabled latebind for dp-42 routing group (rollback step)

Maya (SRE): Commands used:
```
# evict sessions
kubectl -n inference exec router-dp-42 -- /usr/local/bin/routerctl evict --tenant crestline-17
# disable latebind
kubectl -n inference patch configmap routing-config -p '{"data":{"latebind_enabled":"false"}}'
```

Tom (on-call): Leaving the eviction hook active. Please confirm if we should drain dp-42 or failover traffic to dp-43.

Aisha (eng-runtime): Recommend failover to dp-43 for crestline traffic only. Rolling out traffic-rule override to route crestline-17 -> dp-43 with a read-only flag while we validate patch.

Oliver (Solutions): I'll prep a short customer-facing note for Crestline account team. Need confirmation on scope: confirmed affected tenant crestline-17 only or others? I want to avoid alarm until we have clear impact.

Maya (SRE): Initial impact assessment: single reported cross-read events tied to crestline-17 sessions. No signs of broad leakage across other enterprise customers. KV audit shows ~12 anomalous reads between 09:12:23 and 09:14:02 UTC.

Ben (Security): That's consistent with a narrow window. Still treat as potential exposure — start data access audit: which keys were returned, session ids, and whether any PII present.

CI Bot: Running automated KV integrity scrub job (job id: scrub-29655-1). ETA ~14 minutes.

Aisha (eng-runtime): Patch pushed to canary on dp-43 with stricter key encoding. If CI scrub completes clean, will promote and then we can re-enable latebind behind a feature flag.

Maya (SRE): Action items: 
- Ben: continue IR, collect preserved process dump + logs (assigned)
- Aisha: validate patch in dp-43 and provide rollback plan (assigned)
- Tom: keep dp-42 quarantined and hold off drain until we confirm no more anomalies (assigned)
- Oliver: prep customer comms draft for AE to review (assigned)

Oliver (Solutions): Draft for AE — short, technical, apologetic, and next steps. Sending to #customer-comms for review in 15.

Maya (SRE): Will update thread with final status once scrub results and patch validation complete. If CI finds further anomalies we'll escalate to execs and widen the customer notice. For now containment in place. :lock: :white_check_mark:

Incident Bot: Status update scheduled in 10m.
